Introduction: How a Product Marketing &.point: 早期销售本质是布道式产品管理与营销，创始人必须亲自参与
Introduction: How a Product Marketing &.core: At this stage, your “sales” is in large part evangelical product management and product marketing, and this is why you, as a founder, need to be involved in it.
Introduction: How a Product Marketing &.case: For instance, had we embarked on this ill-advised path, we would have likely hired an Account Executive or Sales Manager from LinkedIn. Once hired, he will then call on some of his existing accounts, and secure some early pilots, or worse, maybe even bounce off the purchasing decision maker, and not be able to tell you why. He’ll tell you what the customer said, but likely not what the customer meant. You won’t be able to tell between pure sales failure and product failure.
Introduction: How a Product Marketing &.explain: 从领英挖来的成熟销售只会照搬旧客户名单，碰壁后也说不清是销售失败还是产品失败，无法替创始人完成叙事打磨与倾听迭代。

Chapter 1: Mindset Changes in First Time.point: 既要坚信能赢，又要对被拒绝不为所动
Chapter 1: Mindset Changes in First Time.core: That is, you need to have and project full confidence that you’re going to win the deal, but at the same time be unfazed when you do not.
Chapter 1: Mindset Changes in First Time.case: For whatever reason there won’t be budget, the timing will be off, the prospect will be happy with their current tools, a competitor will win the deal, the prospect will just disappear, etc. It happens. Depending on your industry, and the point at which sales gets a prospect in the funnel, if yours is a new, innovative solution, a 20%–30% win rate is solid.
Chapter 1: Mindset Changes in First Time.explain: 销售中预算不足、时机不对、对手胜出等拒绝是常态；即便新方案，20%–30%赢单率已属稳健，说明需保持必胜信心又不被失单击垮。

Chapter 2: Baking Your Narrative & Produ.point: 叙事第一步是尽量清晰地说出你要解决的业务痛点
Chapter 2: Baking Your Narrative & Produ.core: You need to identify the business pain you’re seeking to solve, as crisply as possible, so your audience can quickly evaluate whether what you’re talking about is relevant to them.
Chapter 2: Baking Your Narrative & Produ.case: For instance, in the case of TalentBin, “Technical recruiting is hard. It’s hard to find software engineering talent that has the relevant skills, and even if you can find them, getting in contact with them is tough. And once you’ve found and contacted talent, keeping on top of all those conversations can be a huge time suck fraught with dropped balls, all leading to slower hire times and raised cost of hire.”
Chapter 2: Baking Your Narrative & Produ.explain: TalentBin 用一段话讲清技术招聘难：难找人、难联系、难跟进，导致招聘变慢、成本上升，听众能立刻判断是否与自己相关。

Chapter 3: Sales Materials Basics: What.point: 在销售演示中放入客户自己的具体信息，最能说明产品能为他做什么
Chapter 3: Sales Materials Basics: What.core: Nothing does that better than using specific customer information in your sales presentation (and later, your demo) to help show that prospect exactly what your solution could do for them.
Chapter 3: Sales Materials Basics: What.case: Their sales deck is set up such that they can drop in Google search results for “working at <prospect company name>” to demonstrate to the prospect what recruiting candidates see when Googling their company. And they have other slides set up to show what a prospect’s career site could look like with LifeGuides-style content deployed.
Chapter 3: Sales Materials Basics: What.explain: LifeGuides 把潜在客户公司的谷歌搜索结果和职业页面直接嵌入幻灯片，让客户看到自己招聘信息在候选人眼中的样子，以及使用产品后的效果，具体而非抽象地证明价值。

Chapter 4: Early Prospecting: Finding Yo.point: 把理想客户画像提炼成可观察特征，判断客户吸引力
Chapter 4: Early Prospecting: Finding Yo.core: You want to get to the point that you can rattle off a set of metadata characteristics that describe the relative level of attractiveness of a prospect.
Chapter 4: Early Prospecting: Finding Yo.case: For instance, in TalentBin’s case, this would be something like “This account has five technical recruiters and twenty open technical hires, including iOS, Java, and Android roles, and uses LinkedIn Recruiter.” What are the characteristics in there? First, we have the existence of technical recruiters—without at least one recruiter or sourcer to actively use the tool, customers are unlikely to have success.
Chapter 4: Early Prospecting: Finding Yo.explain: TalentBin 用技术招聘官人数、开放技术岗位、岗位类型和是否使用 LinkedIn Recruiter 等可观察特征描述账户，说明抽象画像可落成可核对的元数据。

Chapter 5: Prospect Outreach & Demo Appo.point: 外联要多次跟进，且每封邮件都要保持相关性
Chapter 5: Prospect Outreach & Demo Appo.explain: 数据显示第二封邮件回复率最高（18%对首封12%），此后到第五封仍稳定在17%、17%、13%，说明持续且相关的跟进比一次性外联更有效。
Chapter 5: Prospect Outreach & Demo Appo.caseTitle: 冷邮件各封回复率曲线
Chapter 5: Prospect Outreach & Demo Appo.core: They ignore the first outreach—but by sending a second, third, and fourth, and by making sure that those messages are relevant, you can sprint past all those other terrible sales staff.
Chapter 5: Prospect Outreach & Demo Appo.case: the highest response rate to cold outreach emails, based on data from an Outreach study, is to the second email in your drip campaign (18% compared to 12% for first outreach). Response rates then hold steady (17%, 17%, 13%) through the fifth outreach, at which point they start to decline.

Chapter 6: Early Inbound Lead Capture &.point: 入站表单只问判断资格必需、又无法自己查到的信息
Chapter 6: Early Inbound Lead Capture &.core: The biggest thing you’re trying to capture is qualification information and a means by which to get in touch with the person.
Chapter 6: Early Inbound Lead Capture &.case: For instance, at TalentBin, we didn’t ask how many recruiters our inbound requesters had at their organizations, because that was trivial to find on LinkedIn—and every incremental field is a chance for leads to abandon the form. But we did ask how many software engineering roles they were looking to fill in the next six months, since we couldn’t find that on our own and that hiring demand was required for an account to get value out of TalentBin.
Chapter 6: Early Inbound Lead Capture &.explain: TalentBin 不询问 LinkedIn 上可查的招聘官人数，避免多余字段导致放弃；只问无法自行获取、且决定客户能否获益的招聘岗位数，精准筛出合格线索。

Chapter 7: Pitching: Preparation, Presen.point: 需求了解首先要确认对方是否真有你要解决的痛点
Chapter 7: Pitching: Preparation, Presen.core: The most important thing to converge on is whether the prospect has the actual business pain that your solution is seeking to solve. If she doesn’t, this is going to be a useless conversation.
Chapter 7: Pitching: Preparation, Presen.case: Once the prospect had responded to that, we would then cascade further: “Do you find job postings insufficient to get the sort of software engineer applicant flow that you want? Have you had to do passive-candidate recruiting and outreach, for instance via LinkedIn?” If she answered no to this, then we knew the organization may not even have the pain we solved, and we’d have an uphill battle.
Chapter 7: Pitching: Preparation, Presen.explain: TalentBin 在需求了解阶段层层追问：先问招聘信息是否不够用，再问是否需被动候选人寻访。若对方答否，说明其组织可能根本没有该痛点，继续谈只会是艰难而无用的对话。

Chapter 8: Down Funnel Selling: Negotiat.point: 销售阶段要有清晰且对所有人含义一致的定义
Chapter 8: Down Funnel Selling: Negotiat.core: The important thing is that your stages have crisp definitions, and always mean the same thing to you and to anyone else who is using them (i.e., your eventual sales reps).
Chapter 8: Down Funnel Selling: Negotiat.case: Each stage was associated with specific criteria. For instance, “Seeking Approval” was used when pain was validated, and the stakeholder that we were engaged with was interested in proceeding, but there was another stakeholder whose permission or involvement was needed and was being sought. “Sent Proposal” meant that the prospect had specifically requested a proposal to consider pricing options, and that the next step was an up or down decision (or negotiation).
Chapter 8: Down Funnel Selling: Negotiat.explain: TalentBin为每个阶段设定具体标准，如“Seeking Approval”指痛点已验证、对接人有意推进但还需他人批准，使团队对阶段含义理解一致。

Chapter 9: Customer Success Basics: Impl.point: 监测客户不成功的先行指标，在坏习惯固化前介入
Chapter 9: Customer Success Basics: Impl.core: The important thing is to instrument leading indicators of non-success so you can jump on them before that bad or nonexistent usage becomes ingrained.
Chapter 9: Customer Success Basics: Impl.case: On TalentBin, for example, running searches that yield zero results, or unusably large numbers, suggests a problem; we could have designed reporting to alert us to that usage issue, which was likely to block success.
Chapter 9: Customer Success Basics: Impl.explain: TalentBin 把“搜索零结果或结果过多”这类使用异常当作不成功的先行指标，设计报表预警，从而在无效使用固化前及时干预。

Introduction #10.point: 销售动作未被证明可复制前就扩招，会烧钱并伤害公司
Introduction #10.core: Premature scaling involves adding sales staff (or adding many more sales staff) before you have proven that the sales motion actually works.
Introduction #10.case: Some good recent examples of “premature scaling” can be seen in the cautionary tale of Zenefits, who sold epic amounts of deals without fully considering the costs associated with servicing the customers they brought onboard—creating a situation where as reps sold more and more deals, they had more and more negative unit-economic customers on the books bleeding the company dry of resources. Eventually this lead to massive layoffs of these inefficient reps who loaded the company with “upside down” customers.
Introduction #10.explain: Zenefits 在未核算服务成本时就大量成交，销售越多负单位经济客户越多，资源被耗尽，最终大规模裁员低效销售。

Chapter 11: High-Impact Sales Hiring.point: 用模拟真实工作的小作业初筛销售，考察主动性、理解力与执行力
Chapter 11: High-Impact Sales Hiring.explain: 候选人需浏览TalentBin网站提炼价值主张、把Airbnb作为目标客户研究，再录30秒语音推介，这一作品型作业直接暴露其主动性、理解力与执行水平，比空谈简历更能预测实际销售表现。
Chapter 11: High-Impact Sales Hiring.core: For that reason, I’m a particular fan of implementing screens involving the production of some lightweight work artifact as the first step in my hiring process.
Chapter 11: High-Impact Sales Hiring.case: Another artifact-based screen that I like is a mini homework assignment involving account research and voice mail pitching. At the end of the written screen, I tell candidates to leave me a 30-second voice mail, pitching TalentBin as if I were the head of recruiting at Airbnb. Firstly, I like the fact that it’s a composite homework assignment. It requires going to TalentBin’s website and consuming its value propositions, which tests initiative, comprehension, and retention. It also requires qualifying Airbnb as an account, and allows for varying levels of execution on the part of the candidate.

Chapter 12: High-Impact Sales Onboarding.point: 新销售先懂客户业务经济，才能展开顾问式对话
Chapter 12: High-Impact Sales Onboarding.explain: Brad 是前招聘官，用一小时讲透招聘业务，让销售理解客户行业的经济逻辑，这正是顾问式对话的第一步。
Chapter 12: High-Impact Sales Onboarding.core: the first step to being able to have a consultative conversation with a potential client is to understand the base economics of their business.
Chapter 12: High-Impact Sales Onboarding.case: The way that we achieved this at TalentBin was by having one of our sales team, Brad Snider—a former technical recruiter—give a rundown on all things recruiting in a live hour-long class. We called it “The Brad Class.”

Chapter 13: Where Do You Go From Here?.point: 已有销售能像你一样卖出去，再请相近公司的战术型销售负责人
Chapter 13: Where Do You Go From Here?.core: Well, the exit criteria for knowing that you’re ready to hand the reins off to a dedicated sales leader, is that you have a set of sellers who they themselves are successfully selling your solution at least as well as you were.
Chapter 13: Where Do You Go From Here?.case: If you’re a new Business Intelligence (BI) company, then hiring a sales manager or director from Looker, Mode, Domo, etc., is the better bet than hiring one from Tableau, SAP, or Oracle. If you’re a new recruiting solution, it’s the better bet to hire from Greenhouse, Lever, Workable, etc., than from say Oracle, Taleo, SAP, or SuccessFactors.
Chapter 13: Where Do You Go From Here?.explain: 案例用BI公司从Looker、Mode、Domo而非Tableau、SAP、Oracle招销售负责人，说明应选同阶段、同销售模式的战术型负责人，而非大厂背景者。
